Every living thing within a wide radius is compelled to walk toward it, and those who arrive are not killed but kept — reconfigured until nothing remains but praise. The signal coming out of the zone turns out not to be addressed to anyone: it is the congregation, and the advance rate is an appetite.

A: Embryo grading works. It predicts implantation, it is good medicine, and no reasonable person declines it. What nobody intended is that the rubric is an inverse measure of whoever is home — interiority is not the prize but the cost, and the body has been screening in the opposite direction for four billion years. Patients may ask for an ungraded transfer, every clinic honours it, and those children are entirely themselves. The lead embryologist narrates her grading log across one retrieval cycle; she is a graded product herself, scored nine, and mentions it early as a pleasantry.

A: Transit chimes are not music, they are safety signalling with a written design brief: a door-closing tone must produce compliance in about a second and a half, so people clear the doors before they have decided to. Habituation means the spec must be revised to stay ahead of the population that has adapted, each revision working a layer deeper than the last — and the document tracking this since the 1970s is not a design history but a depth gauge, with a fixed floor. Thirty years of exposure removes the interval between stimulus and response, and it generalises.
B: Mission Dolores baptised the dying by the thousand during the epidemics, in Latin and Spanish, to people who spoke Ramaytush and Chochenyo and could not consent, understand, or refuse — and buried them in layers in a plot too small for them, alongside a minority of valid baptisms and a handful of infants the rite could not resolve at all. Two hundred and fifty years later the invalid burials have grown into a single connective mass organised by the sacramental register rather than by anatomy, and it feeds on the one thing in the ground that has the residue of a completed sacrament: the properly baptised, whose bodies are owed back at the resurrection. It has followed the sewer trunks out under the Mission District, and it takes people the city does not file. An archaeological monitor with access to the digitised mission registers is the only person who assembles it, and the document that proves she did is the document that gets her killed.

A: A certified transcript does not describe what happened in the room; it legally *is* what happened, and correcting the paper corrects the event. A court reporter's craft requires training comprehension out — you cannot follow testimony and transcribe at 220 words a minute — so the most authoritative account of what a person said is produced by the only entity in the room that isn't a witness to it. Her error rate rises when she is moved, so her slips cluster where she cared, and eleven years of quiet decency in housing court are eventually paid for with one man.
B: You cannot buy years, only take positions on them — and every position needs a counterparty holding the other side, physically, in a building, under quarterly audit. An independent auditor walks the floor of a legitimate, regulated longevity-futures exchange in real time, dictating against a checklist. Nothing supernatural is required: someone must be short the years someone else is long, and a body is the only warehouse anyone has found. She is not a health inspector; she is verifying the quality of the years.

A: The bay's safety against algal blooms was never ecological virtue but turbidity — an accident of Gold Rush hydraulic mining debris that ran out a century ago. A fully loaded system with the safety off, permanently. The organism needs light and surface area, and a human circulatory system is already an optimal pre-built branching network; it remodels hosts into surface area from the inside out, and their continued life is a design requirement. A hazmat field tech runs the same forty numbered subjects on a fixed route, and subject nineteen has learned the order of her procedure.
